clamp.title: CLAMP, THE WHEEL-CLAMPER
lines: Clamp. A squat yellow thing made entirely of wheel clamps, bolted together into the shape of a very small, very angry traffic warden, with a ticket machine for a head that never stops printing.

He has issued four million parking fines since the first season. Nobody has ever paid one. Not a single fucking penny. He keeps every unpaid ticket in a drift around his ankles, and he's up to his armpits.
He doesn't care that there are no cars on Floor 1. He'll clamp anything. Bins. Goblins. Your legs. He once clamped a man's bollocks to a radiator and walked off whistling.
Strengths: clamps that lock your feet to the floor, tickets fired like shuriken and a bite like a car door. Weaknesses: pay him. Go on. He's never seen money. He won't know what to do.

drowned_valet.title: THE DROWNED VALET
drowned_valet.sub: The Sump. He'll park you somewhere nice and dark.
lines: The Drowned Valet. A bloated corpse in a waterlogged red waistcoat and a little round cap, standing up to his chest in the black water of the Sump, holding out a gloved hand for your keys. He's been holding it out for thirty years.
He parked cars for the Undercroft's first residents, back when it was a real car park, before the flood. When the water came, he stayed at his post. Of course he did. Who'd park the cars?
That card on the notice board offering free spare keys? He wrote it. In his own blood, and some of the Sump. He's lonely. He just wants someone to park.
Strengths: he drags you under, he flings wrecked cars like toys and he stinks so badly your eyes water. Weaknesses: he's very polite. He can't attack while you're tipping him.

agitator.title: THE AGITATOR
agitator.sub: The Drum. Heavy duty. Extra spin.
lines: The Agitator. The beating heart of a washing machine the size of a cathedral: a great twisted spindle of steel paddles, spinning, churning, thrashing in a drum of grey foam, with three contestants still going round in it.
It's been on the same cycle for forty years. Heavy duty. Extra spin. No rinse. Everything it washes comes out cleaner than God and in about nine pieces.
It doesn't think. It doesn't feel. It just agitates. That's its whole name and its whole personality, and honestly, you've been on dates with worse.
Strengths: it spins you, it slams you into the drum and the foam blinds you. Weaknesses: unbalance it. Every washing machine on Earth goes mental when the load's on one side.

trouser_press.title: THE TROUSER PRESS
trouser_press.sub: The Pressing Room. Creases you'll never get out.
lines: The Trouser Press. Two vast iron plates hinged at the back, steaming hot, opening and closing like the jaws of a whale, with an ironing-board tongue and a voice like a posh tailor who's had a stroke.

It presses things. Shirts, trousers, suits, people. It's offered a free pressed suit to every contestant who's walked into the Pressing Room, and every one of them has been pressed. They're on the rails now, flat as pancakes, with a perfect crease down the front.
It takes enormous pride in its work. It's never left a wrinkle in its life. It just doesn't understand why the suits keep screaming.
Strengths: it slams shut, it steams and it flattens. Weaknesses: it can only press what's between the plates. Don't be between the plates. This is the most obvious advice I've ever given.

brisket.title: BRISKET, THE BUTCHER HAG
brisket.sub: The Larder. Fresh in today. That's you.
lines: Brisket. A hag the size of a meat fridge, in a bloodstained apron, with a cleaver in each hand and a necklace of sausages, standing in a larder full of hanging things you really should not look at too closely.
She's Grandma Gristle's sister. She does the meat. Gristle does the soup. Between them, nothing on the Soup District goes to waste, including contestants, especially contestants, mainly contestants.
That job advert for a kitchen hand? She wrote it. She's had nine kitchen hands this season. They're all hanging up behind her. Two of them are mince.

Strengths: cleavers, meat hooks and an appetite that would shame a stag weekend in Magaluf. Weaknesses: she's slow, she's greedy, and she'll stop to sample anything that smells good. Bring a sausage roll.

bone_broth.title: THE BONE BROTH
bone_broth.sub: The Stock Cellar. Simmering since the first season.
lines: The Bone Broth. A cauldron the size of a swimming pool, bubbling in the Stock Cellar, and the broth inside it has stood up, grown arms made of marrow bones and a face made of fat, and started talking.

It's been simmering since the first season. Every bone from every kitchen on the Soup District has gone in. It's the richest, deepest, most flavoursome broth in the dungeon, and it's achieved consciousness, and it's absolutely furious about having been boiled.
The recipe is older than the Network. The password to its cellar is the name of the first ingredient. The first ingredient was a person.
Strengths: scalding splashes, bones thrown like javelins and a smell so good you'll want to drink it mid-fight. Do not drink it mid-fight. Weaknesses: cold. Let it cool and it congeals.

mannequin_bride.title: THE MANNEQUIN BRIDE
mannequin_bride.sub: The Changing Rooms. Something old, something new.
lines: The Mannequin Bride. A shop dummy in a wedding dress, yellowed with age, with a veil that's mostly cobwebs and a bouquet of plastic flowers, standing at the end of a long aisle of changing-room cubicles, waiting.

She was jilted. Well, she was a mannequin, so she was always going to be jilted, but she took it badly. She's been waiting for her groom since the Mall opened. Every contestant who walks into the Changing Rooms, she thinks it's him.
When she realises it isn't, she makes them into mannequins too. Groomsmen. Bridesmaids. A best man who'll never finish his speech. The whole wedding party's here, posed, forever.
Strengths: she's fast, she's hard as plastic and she can turn you into a dummy one limb at a time. Weaknesses: her veil. Find the pieces. She'll stop to put it on.

down_escalator.title: THE DOWN ESCALATOR
down_escalator.sub: The Escalator Shaft. Going down. Always going down.
lines: The Down Escalator. An escalator that has come alive and is extremely hungry, its steps folding into teeth, its handrail lashing like a tongue, rising out of a shaft that goes down further than anyone's ever been able to measure.

It only goes down. It's only ever gone down. Everyone who's stepped on it has gone down with it, and nobody's ever come up. The maintenance sign at the top has been there since the Mall opened. The toolbox it mentions is at the bottom, and it's bait.
It's the Mall Mother's. It's how she disposes of things. Shoplifters. Troublemakers. Contestants who ask about the exits.
Strengths: it drags you down, its steps bite and its handrail grabs. Weaknesses: run up it. Every child in the world knows you can run up a down escalator. It's the one thing it hates.

grill_dad.title: DAD (GRILLING)
grill_dad.sub: The Rec Room. It's not burnt, it's caramelised.
lines: Dad. Specifically, Dad Grilling. A huge man in an apron that says KISS THE COOK, cargo shorts, socks with sandals, and a pair of barbecue tongs he wields like a broadsword, standing over a grill the size of a pickup truck.

He's been running the same barbecue at the Rec Room since Suburbia was built. Everyone's welcome! Grab a plate! The burgers are black. The sausages are black. Some of the guests are black, because he's been grilling them too.
He has opinions about charcoal versus gas. He will share them. He will share them while you're on fire.

Strengths: tongs, flame bursts and dad jokes that do actual psychic damage. Weaknesses: he can't leave the grill. And if you tell him the burgers are lovely, he'll stop and beam for a full five seconds.

lifeguard.title: THE LIFEGUARD
lifeguard.sub: The Pool House. No running. No diving. No coming up.
lines: The Lifeguard. A bronzed, impossibly muscled man in red shorts with a whistle, a float and a zinc-white nose, sitting in a high chair over a swimming pool that's far deeper than it looks.
He's never saved anyone. He's never had to. People drown in his pool, and he blows his whistle, and he says 'no running', and he goes back to staring at the horizon.
There are dozens of people at the bottom of his pool. They're fine. They're just resting. He'll tell you that very firmly if you ask.
Strengths: he drags you under, his whistle stuns you and he swims like a shark that's been on steroids. Weaknesses: the pool bell. Ring it from the high board and he has to clear the pool.

taxidermist.title: THE TAXIDERMIST
taxidermist.sub: The Trophy Hall. You'll look lovely mounted.
lines: The Taxidermist. A thin, wet-lipped man in a leather apron, with glass eyes in a jar on his belt and a needle and thread, standing in a hall full of stuffed contestants, each posed in their most dramatic moment.
He works for the Lodge. Every trophy the hunters take, he mounts. Heads, mostly. Sometimes whole bodies. He's very, very good. His work's been exhibited up there. People have paid millions.
He'll measure you with his eyes as you come in. He's already picked a pose for you. It's undignified. It's mostly arse.
Strengths: hooks, a stuffing gun and stuffed trophies that come back to life when he whistles. Weaknesses: he's precious about his work. Damage a trophy and he'll go to pieces.

alpha.title: ALPHA
alpha.sub: The Kennel Pit. Every good boy, all at once.
lines: Alpha. A dog. Several dogs. Every lost dog in the Wild Kennel, fused into one enormous, many-headed, many-legged hound, still wagging all of its tails, howling with a hundred voices.

They were somebody's good boys. All of them. Pets from Earth, taken with their owners, lost on the Canopy. They found each other in the Kennel Pit, and they wanted so badly to be a pack that they became one, literally, in the most horrible way imaginable.
The 'lost dog' poster on the board? There's a photo on it. It's mostly one dog. The other ninety-nine are just out of frame.
Strengths: a hundred mouths, a hundred legs and a pounce that covers half the pit. Weaknesses: they're still good boys. Tell them to sit. Some of them will.

bailiff.title: THE BAILIFF
bailiff.sub: The Rent Office. Everything you own is now evidence.
lines: The Bailiff. A huge man in a long black coat, with a clipboard, a bunch of keys, a crowbar and a face like a slapped arse, standing in the Rent Office surrounded by everything he's ever repossessed.

He works for the Landlord. He takes things. Furniture, money, clothes, pets, kidneys. He's taken the roof off houses. He's taken the floor out from under people standing on it. He once repossessed a man's trousers while the man was still in them.
He's very calm. He's very reasonable. He'll explain, in a gentle voice, exactly what he's going to take and in which order.
Strengths: he seizes your gear mid-fight, he hits like a door coming off its hinges and the Collectors back him up. Weaknesses: the case number. Quote it to him and he has to check the file.

drowned_debutante.title: THE DROWNED DEBUTANTE
drowned_debutante.sub: The Flooded Ballroom. Her coming-out party never ended.
lines: The Drowned Debutante. A girl in a white ballgown, soaked through, with pondweed in her hair, a dance card on her wrist and mascara running down her cheeks forever, waltzing alone in a ballroom that's two feet underwater.
It was her coming-out party. The Cistern flooded in the middle of the first dance. Everyone else got out. She didn't want to leave without her dance. She's still waiting for someone to ask.
Every contestant who collects a dance card from the door is on her list. She will dance with every one of them. Under the water. Until they stop.
Strengths: she pulls you under, the drowned guests dance around you in a ring and her scream shatters chandeliers. Weaknesses: dance with her. Properly. She'll cry, and let you go.

old_bellows.title: OLD BELLOWS
old_bellows.sub: The Furnace Floor. He breathes fire. On purpose.
lines: Old Bellows. A wrinkled, leathery creature like a giant accordion with legs, wheezing and puffing, with a furnace in his belly and soot pouring out of his mouth every time he breathes, which is constantly, and loudly, like a man climbing stairs after a fry-up.
He keeps the furnaces of the Workings stoked. He's been doing it since the Builders lit them. He breathes in coal dust and breathes out fire, and if he ever stops, the whole floor goes cold.
He's ancient. He's knackered. He's got a cough you can hear three shafts away, and he hawks up lumps of burning coal the size of your fist.
Strengths: fire breath, soot clouds and a body like a bellows. Weaknesses: the dampers. Open them and he can't build up pressure.

foremans_ghost.title: THE FOREMAN'S GHOST
foremans_ghost.sub: Shaft Zero. Shift's not over till he says.
lines: The Foreman's Ghost. A pale, translucent man in a hard hat and a hi-vis vest, with a clipboard and a whistle, floating at the bottom of Shaft Zero, checking his watch.

He was the foreman of the very first shift on the Workings, forty years ago. The shaft collapsed. Everyone died. And he never signed them off, so the shift never ended. All forty-one of his men are still down there with him, still working, forever.
That extra shift on the board? He's still recruiting. He's always short-handed.
Strengths: he calls his dead crew, he throws picks and his whistle makes you work instead of fight. Weaknesses: clock in on his sheet. Then clock out. He'll finally let everyone go.

chief_whip.title: THE CHIEF WHIP
lines: The Chief Whip. A rat. A very large rat, in a pinstripe suit, with a horsewhip in one paw and an order paper in the other, standing in the Council Chamber shouting 'ORDER! ORDER!' at a room full of other rats who are ignoring him.

He keeps the councillors in line. He tells them how to vote. He knows every councillor's secrets, and he keeps them in a little black book, and some of the things in that book would make a sewer wyrm blush.
He's been Chief Whip for nine terms. Nobody likes him. Everybody's terrified of him. That's exactly how he wants it.
Strengths: his whip, his rats and his order paper, which he hits you with surprisingly hard. Weaknesses: the division bell. When it rings, every rat has to go and vote.

auditor.title: THE AUDITOR
auditor.sub: The Counting House. Your accounts are overdue.
lines: The Auditor. A thin, grey man made of ledger paper, with a calculator for a face and fingers like fountain pens, sitting behind a desk in the Counting House, going through your accounts line by line.

He works for Saint Tally, the god of counting. Everything is counted. Everything is recorded. And everything, eventually, is audited. That tax rebate notice with your name already on it? He wrote it. He knew your name because he knows everything.
He's found discrepancies in your accounts. Lots of them. He'll explain them to you very slowly while you bleed out.
Strengths: he audits your buffs away, he throws columns of figures that hurt like knives and he never makes a mistake. Weaknesses: cook his books. One wrong number and he seizes up.

leading_man.title: THE LEADING MAN
leading_man.sub: Stage Zero. It's always been about him.
lines: The Leading Man. A chiselled, impossibly handsome man in a tuxedo, with perfect teeth, perfect hair and a perfect jawline, standing in a spotlight on Stage Zero, delivering a monologue to nobody.

He's the star. He's always been the star. He's been in every episode of every show on the Backlot, and he has never once let anyone else have a line. Every co-star he's ever had has ended up under the stage.
He has a catchphrase. He says it after every kill. It's crap. It's genuinely crap. But the audience goes wild for it.
Strengths: a spotlight that blinds, stunt fighting that looks great on camera and an ego that buffs him. Weaknesses: say his catchphrase before he does. He'll lose his shit.

the_cutter.title: THE CUTTER
the_cutter.sub: The Edit Suite. You won't make the final cut.
lines: The Cutter. A tall, thin figure in a black polo neck with a pair of scissors for hands and strips of film wrapped round its body, standing in the Edit Suite surrounded by bins full of cut footage.

It edits. Every episode, every scene, every contestant. It decides what stays and what goes. And what goes, goes. Snip. Gone. Every contestant who was ever cut from the show is in those bins, in tiny strips of film, still moving.
That screening of your deleted scenes? It's real. It's just that you're about to be one.
Strengths: scissors that cut through anything, jump-cuts that teleport it and the ability to edit your attacks out. Weaknesses: the film. Without footage, it's got nothing to cut.

the_manager.title: THE MANAGER
the_manager.sub: The Dugout. Sacked nine times. Still here.
lines: The Manager. A red-faced man in a long coat with a clipboard, chewing gum like it owes him money, standing in the dugout screaming at players who aren't there.
He's been sacked nine times. Every time, he comes back. Nobody knows how. He just turns up the next season in the dugout, chewing, swearing, with a new tactical philosophy he's read in a book.
He's convinced he's one more season away from greatness. He's not. He's been relegated from three different dimensions.
Strengths: he throws water bottles like grenades, calls in his subs and his half-time team talk buffs everything around him. Weaknesses: the floodlights. In the dark, he can't see the tactics board.

the_replay.title: THE REPLAY
the_replay.sub: The Replay Room. Let's see that again.
lines: The Replay. A figure made of flickering television screens, each one showing the same moment over and over: a goal, a foul, a fall, a contestant dying, from every angle, in slow motion.

It replays. Everything. Every fight you've had, it's watched, and it can do all your moves, frame by frame, because it's seen them a hundred times. It's seen you trip. It's seen you cry. It's seen you shit yourself in the Ticket Hall, and it's watched that one forty times.
It wants your highlight tape. It wants to add you to the reel.
Strengths: it replays your own attacks back at you, in slow motion, at full damage. Weaknesses: do something new. Lose on purpose. It's never seen that.

the_face.title: THE FACE
the_face.sub: The Makeup Chair. Everyone's face, at once.
lines: The Face. A shape in the makeup chair, under a sheet, that, when the sheet comes off, is a body wearing every face anyone's ever had done in Hair and Makeup, all at once, stitched together, blinking out of sync.
Every face the Makeup Witch ever got wrong ended up here. Every bad makeover. Every botched contour. They all crawled into the chair together and became this.
It wants your face. It's not fussy. Any face will do. It'll take yours and add it to the collection, right between a newsreader and somebody's nan.
Strengths: it wears your face to confuse you, it screams with a hundred mouths and it grabs. Weaknesses: water. Makeup runs. So do the faces.

ghostwriter.title: THE GHOSTWRITER
ghostwriter.sub: The Writers' Bunker. He's already written your ending.
lines: The Ghostwriter. A pale, transparent man hunched over a typewriter in a bunker full of crumpled paper, typing, always typing, with ink-stained fingers and a cigarette that never burns down.
He writes the Network's scripts. All of them. Every season. Every contestant's story. He's written yours already. He's written how you die. He's very proud of it. It's on page forty-three.
He's never met a single contestant. He doesn't want to. It's easier to write people when you never have to look at them.
Strengths: he writes your moves before you make them, he types up obstacles and his ink spills blind you. Weaknesses: the last pages. Steal them and he doesn't know how it ends.

first_edition.title: THE FIRST EDITION
first_edition.sub: The Rare Books Room. Do not touch. Do not read. Do not.
lines: The First Edition. A book. An enormous, ancient book, bound in something that might be leather and might be skin, lying open on a lectern under three reading lamps, its pages turning by themselves.

It's the first book ever written in the Stack. By the Builders. It's in no language you know. If you read it, you'll understand it. And understanding it does things to your brain that you won't enjoy.
It doesn't like to be touched without gloves. It doesn't like to be touched at all. It doesn't like you.
Strengths: it reads you, it turns its pages into blades and it rewrites your abilities. Weaknesses: the reading lamps. Turn them off. A book can't do anything in the dark.

hush.title: HUSH
lines: Hush. A tall, pale, featureless figure with a single enormous finger pressed to where its lips would be, standing in the Quiet Room, in absolute silence.
It is silence. It's the silence of the Stacks made solid. Every sound that's ever been shushed in this library went somewhere, and that somewhere is here, and it's this.
That library card with your photo on it? It's yours. It's always been yours. It was waiting for you before you were born. Collect it quietly.
Strengths: absolute silence that drains your abilities, and a shush that can stop your heart. Weaknesses: noise. Any noise. Scream. Swear. Fart. Fart as loud as you can. It'll hate it.

iron_maiden.title: THE IRON MAIDEN
iron_maiden.sub: The Torture Exhibit. The exhibits will touch you.
lines: The Iron Maiden. A spiked iron coffin in the shape of a woman, seven feet tall, standing in the middle of Castle Dread's Torture Exhibit, opening and closing her door with a creak like a slow, delighted laugh.

She's the star exhibit. Every torture device in Castle Dread is on display in this hall, with a little placard explaining how it works. She's the only one that still works. And she's ever so keen to demonstrate.
She was a prop. A fake. The spikes were rubber. Then the castle kept running, and decided she ought to be real, and she's been making up for lost time ever since.
Strengths: spikes, a crushing embrace and the rack, the wheel and the chair all following her orders. Weaknesses: her keys. Lock her door shut.

the_banquet.title: THE BANQUET
the_banquet.sub: The Banquet Hall. As the main course.
lines: The Banquet. A dining table forty feet long, laden with rotten food, that has stood up on its legs, with a mouth where the head of the table should be and cutlery for teeth, inviting you to dinner. As dinner.

It's the Count's great hall. Every night, the banquet scene plays out: the guests arrive, the food is served, and the guests become the food. The table's been doing it for forty years. It's absolutely stuffed.
Your place card is waiting. You're seated between a skeleton and a man with an apple in his mouth.
Strengths: plates thrown like discuses, a mouth that swallows you whole and a food fight that is literally deadly. Weaknesses: table manners. Dress for dinner, and it has to treat you as a guest.

corrupted_save.title: THE CORRUPTED SAVE
lines: The Corrupted Save. A glitching, flickering figure, half-loaded, its body missing pieces, with a progress bar stuck at 99% floating over its head and a voice that stutters, 'L-l-loading...'

It's a contestant's save file. A real one. Someone who came down here, seasons ago, and tried to back themselves up in the Builders' memory. The backup got corrupted. And now it's stuck forever, trying to load, never quite making it.
It doesn't remember its name. It remembers bits. A dog. A kitchen. A song. It's trying so hard to remember the rest.
Strengths: it glitches through attacks, corrupts your abilities and resets the fight. Weaknesses: restore its backups. Give it its memories back.

frost_kernel.title: THE FROST KERNEL
lines: The Frost Kernel. A tiny, glowing blue core, no bigger than a fist, floating above a lake of liquid coolant, surrounded by a storm of ice that's taken the shape of a giant.
It's the heart of the Cold Store's cooling. Every server in the Stack is kept cold by this little blue light. It's ancient. It's ridiculously powerful. And it's lonely as hell.
That heater core in the service bay? It's bait. The Kernel knows warm things come to warm things.
Strengths: ice storms, freezing beams and armour of ice it can regrow. Weaknesses: drain the coolant. No lake, no ice.

the_chroma.title: THE CHROMA
the_chroma.sub: The Green Screen. Now you see it.
lines: The Chroma. A shape you can only see the edges of, against the vast green screen of the Transmitter's studio, because it's exactly the same colour as the screen. Bright, flat, nauseating green.
It's a keyed-out monster. Everything that's ever been filmed in front of the green screen and removed in post ended up here. It's what's left when you take everything out of a picture.
It can be anywhere on the screen. It can be anything. It can be right behind you. It is right behind you.
Strengths: invisibility against green, sudden appearances and it can put anything in the background. Weaknesses: the one green thing that's real. Find it. Ring the studio bell.

vision_mixer.title: THE VISION MIXER
vision_mixer.sub: The Vision Mixer's Desk. Camera three.
lines: The Vision Mixer. A woman with six arms, each hand on a fader, sitting at a desk covered in buttons, switching between cameras so fast the screens are a blur, screaming 'CAMERA THREE! CAMERA THREE!'
She decides what the audience sees, second by second. She cuts between shots. She makes the drama. She has never had a break, never had lunch, never been to the toilet. She has a bag. Don't ask.
Your mark is on her desk. She's been waiting for you to stand on it.
Strengths: she cuts between angles, teleporting around the room, and she can make you vanish from the shot. Weaknesses: she can only cut to what's on camera. Stay off camera three.

baby_host.title: BABY HOST
baby_host.sub: The Nursery. Look who's a big boy now.
lines: Baby Host. The Host, aged two. In a nappy, in a cot, in the Nursery of his childhood home, with his famous smile already on his little face. Except he's twelve feet tall.
He's the first memory. The Host's earliest moment. And even then, the cameras were on him. His mother filmed everything. He learned to smile for the lens before he learned to walk.
He wants his rattle. He's always wanted his rattle. And that babysitting job is very, very easy, if you don't mind a toddler the size of a house screaming for it.
Strengths: tantrums that shake the room, a bottle that sprays and a nappy that you really, really do not want him to sit on. Weaknesses: his rattle. Find it.

under_the_bed.title: THE THING UNDER HIS BED
under_the_bed.sub: The Bedroom. He was always afraid of it. He was right.
lines: The Thing Under His Bed. Long, thin, black, all arms and fingers, with eyes that glow when the nightlights go out, curled up beneath the Host's childhood bed. It's been there since he was five.
He was afraid of it. Every night. His mother told him it wasn't real. She was wrong. It was very real, and it's still here, and it's been waiting for him to come home for sixty years.
It's the only thing in the Host's whole life that he's ever been truly afraid of. Understand it, and you'll understand him.

Strengths: it lives in the dark, it grabs from below and its fingers are everywhere at once. Weaknesses: the light. Turn the nightlights off. Wait. What? No, you want them ON. Why would you turn them off? Oh. Oh no.

doorkeeper.title: THE DOORKEEPER
doorkeeper.sub: The Antechamber. There was always a door.
lines: The Doorkeeper. A tall, robed figure with a key for a face, standing in a bare concrete room in front of a plain grey door. It's been standing there since the beginning of everything.
The door leads to the Builders' Seat. Nobody gets through without the knock. The knock is very old. The Builders made it up. Very few people have ever known it.
It doesn't fight to kill. It fights to make sure you're meant to be here. And honestly, nobody is.
Strengths: it locks you in, it locks you out and it can lock your abilities. Weaknesses: the knock. Learn it. Use it.

every_previous_host.title: EVERY PREVIOUS HOST
every_previous_host.sub: The Hall of Winners. Thank you, and goodnight.
lines: Every Previous Host. Not one figure, but dozens: every Host there's ever been, every winner who sat in the chair, standing together in the Hall of Winners, smiling, in their suits, from every era of the Network.
Winning makes you the Host. When a new Host takes over, the old one comes here. All of them are here. They've been here for centuries. Smiling. Waiting. Introducing each other, over and over.
That award with your name embossed in gold? It's real. You've won. You're the next one. This is the hall you'll be standing in.
Strengths: they're all the Host, and they all fight like the Host. Weaknesses: read their names. Every one. They've forgotten them. Remind them.
